cohortDefinition: Twenty distinct source-listed FDA approval decisions dated September 1–30, 2026, regardless of originally scheduled PDUFA goal date. This is NOT the same as September-goal-date calendar: pdufa.bio separately lists 23 September target/quarter rows, which include early decisions, duplicates/partners and non-September decisions.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Single-study rare-neurology program with reported functional benefit; phase and complete statistical package need independent verification
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Severe Alexander disease without established disease-modifying treatment; safety exposure and motor endpoint validation unresolved
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: FDA accepted NDA for priority review, with September 22 goal; rare-disease regulatory flexibility favors review but is not a guarantee
predecision.criticalUnverified: Small rare disease trial, clinical meaningfulness, manufacturing and postapproval obligations

rows.phaseFirstContext: Pivotal Alexander disease trial; Phase 3-style rare-disease comparison
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Reported 10-meter walk test stabilization versus control; nominal endpoint analysis requires multiplicity audit
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Adverse events and long-term intrathecal exposure need complete review
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Priority review and high unmet need support approval; one pivotal rare-disease trial remains a generalizability risk
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Positive randomized PFS for ESR1 molecular switch; mature survival benefit not established at the decision point
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Early molecular switching may delay progression, but the actual patient benefit and rhythm-related risks need confirmation
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: FDA's April 2026 oncology advisory committee did not yield a favorable majority and May extension requested further data; conservative risk-lean is CRL even though accelerated approval remained possible
predecision.criticalUnverified: Regulatory disagreement; additional data; accelerated pathway could reverse the negative lean

rows.phaseFirstContext: Phase 3 SERENA-6 randomized double-blind, ctDNA-guided switching
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: PFS HR 0.44 and P<0.00001 favored camizestrant-CDK4/6; OS immature
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Tolerability of endocrine/CDK4/6 combinations and diagnostic population limits need review
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Strong progression-free survival and companion diagnostic favor approval; accelerated pathway and OS immaturity increase risk
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: 187-person randomized placebo-controlled Phase 3 Ameluz PDT study; sponsor reported significant primary and secondary endpoints in October 2024
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Non-surgical sBCC local therapy with established prior actinic-keratosis platform; full recurrence data and safety need inspection
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: Prior marketed therapy plus positive U.S. pivotal study supports a supplemental indication approval lean
predecision.criticalUnverified: Durability, histologic clearance, photosensitization and manufacturing inspection not independently checked

rows.phaseFirstContext: Randomized double-blind Phase 3 Ameluz/PDT trial in sBCC
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Sponsor-reported primary/secondary p<0.0001 in 187 patients
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Dermatologic tolerability, recurrence follow-up and device-lamp compatibility require review
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Existing Ameluz approval plus highly positive indication trial support supplement; device labeling and CMC remain unresolved
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: First-line HER2-mutant NSCLC cohort in Phase 1/2 SOHO-01, not a completed Phase 3; prior drug has accelerated later-line approval
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Rare oncogene-directed population; single-arm response duration/selection bias and confirmatory evidence unresolved
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: FDA granted priority review May 18, 2026 for first-line supplement; prior approved molecule favors a cautious accelerated-approval lean
predecision.criticalUnverified: Single arm, small subgroups, no mature randomized OS and confirmatory trial requirement

rows.phaseFirstContext: SOHO-01 Phase I/II nonrandomized first-line cohort; not a Phase 3 trial
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Predecision public source described promising HER2-mutant NSCLC response evidence but comparative survival was immature
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Small nonrandomized cohort and durability/toxicity remain uncertain
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Existing prior-line accelerated approval and granted Priority Review support first-line expansion; confirmatory obligation remains risk
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: PET imaging agent evidence, not a Phase 3 drug-efficacy trial in the therapeutic sense; validated diagnostic performance still needs original assessment
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Distinguishing recurrent glioma from treatment-related changes is an unmet diagnostic need
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: FDA accepted resubmitted NDA with September 11 goal; familiar FET-PET practice in international guidelines favors approval
predecision.criticalUnverified: Original diagnostic accuracy, manufacturing, imaging reproducibility and pediatric extrapolation unresolved

rows.phaseFirstContext: Radiopharmaceutical imaging diagnostic clinical-development package
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Clinical need to distinguish recurrent glioma from treatment effect; pivotal diagnostic test accuracy needs independent analysis
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Radiation exposure, reader agreement and comparator standards require review
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: FDA accepted a resubmitted NDA after earlier CRL; reopened review and international clinical use support cautious approval lean, but CMC/technical gaps remain
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Positive pivotal SMA study supports efficacy; not regraded from original SAP
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Previously identified third-party fill-finish OAI and CRL represent major independent CMC risk; no assumption that efficacy resolves facilities
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: August 21 announcement says FDA-guided removal of failing fill-finish plant and alternate facility review; approval lean, with high conditional CMC risk
predecision.criticalUnverified: Alternate-facility readiness and inspection outcome unknown before decision

rows.phaseFirstContext: Phase 3 SAPPHIRE plus spinal muscular atrophy background SMN-targeting treatment
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Sponsor describes positive motor-function efficacy and revised BLA with standard safety update
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Long-term muscle-function durability and concomitant background treatment need review
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Prior BLA issues centered on additional fill-finish site; accepted resubmission/priority designations support approval if manufacturing is fixed
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Small single-arm pediatric PK/PD and safety study with prior randomized efficacy precedent in older population
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Weight/exposure limits required narrowing to at least 27 kg; previous lower-weight risk cannot be extrapolated away
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: June 4 resubmission acceptance after Jan CRL and analytical-method amendments provides conditional approval lean; reused from October action/goal crossover
predecision.criticalUnverified: Second lower-weight sNDA is separate; original CMC method acceptance remains a risk

rows.phaseFirstContext: Small pediatric open-label PK/PD-safety bridge with earlier adolescent indication
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Prior adult/adolescent efficacy plus dose/exposure pediatric rationale; not a new blinded Phase 3 efficacy RCT
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Lower-weight underexposure and production analytical-method issue caused January 2026 CRL
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Resubmission excludes under-27kg children and supplied analytical-method response; approval lean for narrowed indication; earlier CRL remains material risk
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Placebo-controlled FINE-ONE reported UACR improvement; clinical kidney-outcome benefit extrapolated from T2D CKD trials
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: T1D CKD high unmet need; hyperkalemia and extrapolation beyond UACR remain concerns
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: May 21 accepted priority-review supplemental application and established marketed compound support approval lean
predecision.criticalUnverified: UACR is a surrogate; direct kidney-outcome proof and safety need independent evaluation

rows.phaseFirstContext: FINE-ONE Phase 3 242 adults T1D with CKD, placebo-controlled
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Finerenone reduced urine albumin-creatinine ratio versus placebo; surrogate-endpoint extrapolation to kidney outcomes must be scrutinized
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Hyperkalemia 10.1% versus 3.3%, with potential eGFR changes; monitor renal function
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Prior type 2 CKD outcomes + strong albuminuria signal support indication extension, but surrogate acceptance and hyperkalemia risk remain
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Prior ROS1+ NSCLC indication approved; proposed supplement updates duration-of-response data from TRUST-I/II, not a new pivotal indication
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Longer follow-up may show sustained response but publication heterogeneity, exact counts and censoring require review
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: May 6, 2026 FDA acceptance of a postmarketing sNDA with Jan 2027 goal supports label update approval lean; September FDA action was early
predecision.criticalUnverified: Early action cannot be inferred from predecision evidence; not a September PDUFA-goal event

rows.phaseFirstContext: Two Phase 2 single-arm TRUST-I and TRUST-II, existing June 2025 label
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Predecision longer-follow-up response duration and objective responses support label update, but not comparative survival benefit
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: CNS activity and serious toxicity require ongoing exposure reconciliation
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Existing marketing authorization and updated follow-up data favor supplemental label update; no new efficacy indication or phase 3 inferred
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Rare pediatric MPS IIIA gene-therapy program, proposed surrogate-based accelerated review; absence of fully established clinical endpoints remains material
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Neurodevelopmental progression and long-term safety of AAV gene therapy require careful independent examination
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: FDA accepted April 2 resubmitted BLA with September 19 goal after earlier FDA deficiency; conditional approval lean recognizing progress and unmet need
predecision.criticalUnverified: Prior CRL, vector durability, biodistribution, CMC and confirmatory obligations could reverse call

rows.phaseFirstContext: Small uncontrolled AAV9 gene therapy studies and natural-history comparison in Sanfilippo type A
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Long-term biomarker CSF-HS improvements and neurodevelopmental observations, not randomized Phase 3 replication
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Durability, delayed AAV toxicities and exposure heterogeneity remain significant risks
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: FDA accepted resubmitted accelerated-approval BLA April 2026 after earlier response; reasonable rare-disease approval lean, but clinical surrogate and CMC uncertain
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Randomized EMBER-3 reported stronger PFS with imlunestrant/abemaciclib; OS multiplicity criterion not met for every comparison
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Endocrine-resistant ESR1-mutated disease benefits from additional oral targeted options; toxicity of CDK4/6 combination persists
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: December 2025 published sponsor clinical update supported a targeted combination approval lean; exact indication must be preserved
predecision.criticalUnverified: Clinical benefit extrapolation, companion diagnostic, survival hierarchy and hepatic or hematologic safety

rows.phaseFirstContext: Phase 3 randomized EMBER-3 endocrine breast cancer study
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: PFS benefit with imlunestrant-abemaciclib versus imlunestrant; ESR1 subset and multiplicity require precise indication mapping
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Combination diarrhea, neutropenia and other CDK4/6 risks require labeling controls
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Established abemaciclib risk-management and positive PFS support indication amendment; OS immature and restricted biomarker label likely
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Prior drug approved in 2024 and 2025, but original S-017 June 2026 filing, safety update details and FDA interactions not identified in predecision sources examined
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Existing PAH efficacy does not settle new bleeding/hypersensitivity labeling changes; exact clinical effect for specific supplement cannot be graded
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: Source alone lacks predecision S-017 scope and agency review; abstain rather than guess on a safety-label supplement
predecision.criticalUnverified: Need June 2026 S-017 submission or contemporaneous sponsor 8-K and source as published

rows.phaseFirstContext: ZENITH Phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled high-risk PAH; existing sotatercept approval
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Early-stopped trial met morbidity/mortality composite; preserve hierarchy and component analysis
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Bleeding, thrombocytopenia and erythrocytosis risks require full safety and dose monitoring
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Strong second positive Phase 3 and pre-existing PAH authorization favor supplement; clinical subgroup and label scope still need FDA review
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: QWINT-1/2/3/4 demonstrated non-inferior HbA1c versus daily basal insulin, including predecision 2025 journal and sponsor reporting
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Weekly dose simplifies treatment but hypoglycemia and high-dose dosing errors require care; T1D results should not be imputed to approved T2D population
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: 2025 robust multi-study noninferiority makes a T2D-only approval lean defensible
predecision.criticalUnverified: Long-term hypoglycemia, type 1 vs type 2 labeling distinction and CMC

rows.phaseFirstContext: QWINT-2 and QWINT-4 Phase 3 basal-insulin comparisons
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Once-weekly basal efsitora reported noninferior HbA1c reduction versus daily insulin
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Hypoglycemia and dosing error/missed-dose safety require additional risk management
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Multiple positive noninferiority studies and established comparator pathway support approval; dosing-device/regulatory CMC unverified
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Randomized trial reported PFS HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.59–0.84; interim OS HR 0.85, P=0.06075 not formally positive
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Benefit on PFS with safety risks anemia/hypoxia and immature OS
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: Merck/Eisai Feb 28, 2026 disclosure says FDA accepted two sNDAs and set October 4 target; approval lean grounded in primary PFS despite OS caution
predecision.criticalUnverified: Approval Sep 24 early relative to October goal; avoid counting goal-month and action-month as separate trials

rows.phaseFirstContext: LITESPARK-011 Phase 3 randomized advanced RCC versus cabozantinib
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: PFS significant on one dual-primary endpoint; OS not proven, so no survival superiority claim
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Combination anemia, hypoxia and hypertension/other TKI harms necessitate risk assessment
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Existing individual drug approvals, PFS signal and FDA supplemental acceptance favor restricted PFS-based indication, OS uncertainty constrains benefit claim
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: INShore was publicly identified as Phase 3 in contemporaneous trial filings, but original locked efficacy hierarchy and source-as-of decision not independently recovered in this review
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Steroid-dependent pediatric nephrotic syndrome involves infection and B-cell suppression risk; safety subgroup and immunosuppression exposure require review
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: The study existed before September; evidence available in this workpaper is insufficient to reconstruct an exact FDA-cycle regulatory lean
predecision.criticalUnverified: Obtain date-stamped predecision INShore topline and original protocol/SAP rather than importing approval-day statistics

rows.phaseFirstContext: INShore Phase 3 randomized obinutuzumab versus mycophenolate mofetil (prior positive program referenced in February statement)
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Predecision sponsor referenced positive idiopathic nephrotic syndrome study, but this source does not publish numerical INShore effect size
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Anti-CD20 immunosuppression, infections and long-term relapse control require review
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Existing anti-CD20 licensure and referenced positive INShore study support approval lean; no outcome-day label numbers used as predecision evidence
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Randomized placebo-controlled pivotal PROGRESS Phase 2 in FOP, not Phase 3; reported reduced HO lesion formation and tolerability
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Rare disease and serious heterotopic ossification; surrogate lesion measures and pediatric extension uncertain
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: July 2026 public results plus accepted priority-review NDA with September 26 target support conditional approval lean
predecision.criticalUnverified: Small trial, nominal P-values for exploratory endpoints and possible CMC gaps

rows.phaseFirstContext: PROGRESS pivotal Phase 2 randomized rare-disease trial, NOT Phase 3
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Prespecified new-lesion incidence comparison 1/32 vs 5/31 reported P=0.0986; favorable lesion-volume comparisons nominal P<0.0001
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Short placebo window and rare-disease sample limit confidence; favorable safety reported
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: A Level 3 skeptical reviewer would lean CRL on missed key primary test despite favorable secondary volume; FDA regulatory flexibility can overturn this risk lean
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: TEMPO-1/2/3 reported significant motor/daily functioning improvement across early and advanced Parkinson disease
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Clinical functioning benefit plausible, but longer-term dyskinesia, sedation and neuropsychiatric events need review
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: Sep 26, 2025 NDA submission after three successful Phase 3 trials supports approval lean
predecision.criticalUnverified: Three related trials are not independent FDA decisions; dossier safety/CMC unverified

rows.phaseFirstContext: TEMPO-3 Phase 3 randomized add-on levodopa; parallel Phase 3 monotherapy program
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Met primary ON-time without troublesome dyskinesia by +1.1 hours versus placebo, P<0.0001
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Dopamine agonist neuropsychiatric and dyskinesia effects require full safety review
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Positive randomized movement-symptom evidence and larger program support approval; overall monotherapy endpoint detail still unreviewed
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Registered 2026-09-08 Phase 3 pediatric alopecia study, but at that point public pediatric primary readout not independently confirmed in this workpaper
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Adult baricitinib efficacy precedes adolescent indication; class JAK risks infection, thrombosis and cardiovascular events remain
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: Without predecision pediatric efficacy analysis and label-specific risk review, do not infer decision from adult authorization
predecision.criticalUnverified: Need frozen registry version, prespecified pediatric efficacy/safety and label indication boundary

rows.phaseFirstContext: BRAVE-AA-PEDS Phase 3 randomized pediatric alopecia trial (registry snapshot)
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Clinical trial registered placebo-controlled SALT-based endpoint; specific treatment-group efficacy not validated from a dated predecision publication
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Baricitinib has boxed warnings for serious infections, malignancy, MACE and thrombosis; pediatric extrapolation uncertain
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Established adult alopecia baricitinib approval and Phase 3 pediatric study support low-confidence expansion lean; predecision endpoint result unverified
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: March 2026 Ponlimsi approval documents same denosumab-adet for different reference product, Prolia, but not Degevma-specific Xgeva interchangeability analytic package
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Biosimilar pathway supports concept; product-specific interchangeability/extrapolated indications and manufacturing require verification
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: No original predecision Degevma reference-product analytical comparison and sponsor CMC package inspected; abstain
predecision.criticalUnverified: Do not count other Teva biosimilar approval as proof of this application

rows.phaseFirstContext: Biosimilar 351(k) analytical comparability pathway, not a novel Phase 3 efficacy application
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Same active denosumab-adet substance already licensed March 2026 as Ponlimsi for Prolia reference; Degevma Xgeva strength/indications still require independent comparability
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Hypocalcemia, osteonecrosis and biosimilar manufacturing consistency require review
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Prior 60-mg biosimilar license makes additional 120-mg reference product plausible but BLA 761481 CMC/interchangeability not public in predecision source
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

predecision.level1ClinicalEvidence: Randomized 28-week SCOUT-HCM Phase 3 in adolescents met primary LVOT gradient endpoint; adult Camzyos evidence previously established
predecision.level2BenefitRisk: Small pediatric study and cardiac systolic dysfunction risk; REMS/echo monitoring important
predecision.level3RegulatoryFit: January 12 positive topline plus June 1 FDA priority-review acceptance favor carefully restricted pediatric indication approval
predecision.criticalUnverified: Pediatric weight bounds, reduced LVEF and labeling/REMS controls

rows.phaseFirstContext: SCOUT-HCM Phase 3 randomized pediatric trial in symptomatic oHCM, n=44
rows.level1TrialAndEfficacy: Predecision sponsor statement says trial met primary LVOT gradient endpoint; modest size and functional benefit need review
rows.level2SafetyAndCounterevidence: Known adult mavacamten LVEF reduction risk, echocardiographic monitoring/REMS pediatric applicability uncertain
rows.level3RegulatoryFit: Existing adult indication and positive pediatric randomized endpoint support extension; pediatric exposure and REMS adjustments remain caution
rows.decisionLeakageDisclosure: Assessor knew the eventual FDA decision before writing this November 2026 reconstruction.

historicalControls: Every research assessment was created in November 2026 after FDA September outcomes were known. Cited source-publication dates are before action dates, but original-source text has not been independently version-sealed; author was outcome-exposed. Do not represent the resulting 19/20 agreement as measured prediction accuracy, calibrated probability, or proof of model skill. Always APPROVAL comparator scores 20/20 (100%) on this selected all-approval action-date cohort. Not an exhaustive September goal-date PDUFA cohort. Do not add to prospective scoring or October independent accuracy.
priorHistoricalCrossMonthNote: PHAR was cross-referenced from October historical target-date study but now also receives a source-dated expanded summary here. This is one shared case, not a new independent observation.
researchMethod: 20 evidence-date-restricted Level 1/2/3 narratives reconstructed after September outcomes were publicly known; date claims for press releases are documentary dates not verified immutable publication timestamps. The 20 source-index FDA approvals were selected ex post and do not constitute a representative calendar of September PDUFA target actions or CRLs. Claims never promoted to independent blind tests.
